title: Rapid customer snapshot and replay options
summary: Short technical snapshot for customers: On 2029-04-20 02:14 UTC we detected a routing regression affecting a subset of EU-serving inference pools which caused elevated tail latency and, for ~0.6% of requests, duplicated partial responses. The root cause is a misapplied routing rule during a rollout that sent concurrent requests to both the primary and a fallback model variant for affected tenants. No data was exfiltrated; duplicated content is limited to model outputs. This document outlines a concise customer-facing status update, consent-based replay options, and operator steps for evidence and verification.
customer_message:
Status update (suitable for status.redwood.ai):

- Incident ID: INC-4291
- Impact: Elevated latency and occasional duplicate/partial responses for a small subset of requests in EU region between 02:14–02:44 UTC on 2029-04-20.
- Current status: Mitigated — routing rule reverted and no further duplication observed after 02:44 UTC.
- Service impact: API endpoints remained available; some requests experienced higher latency and in rare cases returned duplicated fragments that should not affect downstream data stores.
- What we did: Rolled back the faulty routing rule, validated request routing, and ran targeted verification checks on affected pools.
- What you can do: If you observed duplicated outputs that need reconciliation, you can opt into a guided replay of affected request windows (details below) or use our self-serve verification checklist.
- Next update: We will send a follow-up with a curated evidence package and optional replay choices within 48 hours.

If you need expedited help, contact your customer success lead or open a Priority support ticket.
replay_options: Option A — Self-serve evidence bundle: We provide a timestamped bundle containing request ids, request timestamps, and sanitized outputs for the affected window. No reprocessing is performed. Customers can use this to locally reconcile duplicates.

Option B — Guided selective replay (consent required): With your permission we will replay only requests that failed integrity checks or returned duplicates into a read-only replay environment. We will not persist any new user data and will provide logs for verification. Replay is best if you want us to re-evaluate outputs with the corrected routing (tradeoff: delays of 1–3 business days).

Option C — Full automated remediation (enterprise only): For customers on Dedicated/Private plans we can run an automated reconcile that detects duplicated outputs and either delete or annotate them in-place according to your policy (requires pre-existing integration, takes 3–5 days).
operator_notes: Primary mitigation: rollback routing rule r-2029-04-eu-02 applied at 02:44 UTC. Confirmed no additional concurrent routing after rollback.
Verification steps executed: consumer-side ping tests, KV cache flush validation, sample request trace replays, and model-variant concordance checks across affected hosts.

Evidence packaging: generate CSV of affected request ids, small sanitized payloads (truncate PII), and per-request trace IDs. Store evidence bundle in internal S3 path with read-only link to customer after approval.
Escalation: pass to SRE-runbook for long-tail latency if spikes reoccur. Flag for postmortem in infra-team backlog with tag infra-routing-2029.
Owner for customer comms: Aisha Patel (CS). Operator lead: Marcus Chen (SRE).
timeline: 2029-04-20 02:14 UTC — Rollout of routing change began (automated canary).
2029-04-20 02:18 UTC — Alerts triggered for increased 99th percentile latency in eu-rr pool.
2029-04-20 02:22 UTC — First customer reports of duplicated partial outputs.
2029-04-20 02:30 UTC — Engineering paused rollout and began investigation.
2029-04-20 02:44 UTC — Rollback of routing rule completed; mitigation confirmed.
2029-04-20 03:10 UTC — Targeted verification checks completed; no further duplicates observed.
evidence_instructions: How customers can request and review evidence: 1) Reply to this communication or open a support ticket referencing INC-4291 and state preferred option (A/B/C). 2) For Option A we will share a time-limited S3 link with a README and CSV manifest. 3) For Option B we will provide a consent form that lists the exact request id ranges and the scope of the replay; you must approve within 5 business days. 4) Evidence artifacts are sanitized: we redact obvious PII and token-level embeddings; customers needing raw artifacts must have an approved DPA addendum in place.
next_steps_and_slas: Within 48h — Publish full customer-facing post-incident summary and attach evidence bundle (Option A ready).
Within 5 business days — Begin guided replays for customers who selected Option B after consent is received.
Within 10 business days — Internal RCA published to infra and product teams with remediation plan (auto-tests for routing rollout).

SLA notes: This incident does not qualify for credit under the standard availability SLA because endpoints were reachable; customers may request a commercial review for cases with demonstrable business impact.
faq_snippets: Q: Was customer data exposed? A: No data was exfiltrated. The issue duplicated model outputs; we have not detected any external access to customer data beyond standard API logs.
Q: Will replays change my stored data? A: Replays are read-only unless you opt into automated remediation. We never write back to your production stores without explicit agreement.
Q: How long will the evidence be available? A: Evidence bundles are available for 30 days after we share them unless you request extended access.
Q: Do I need to take action? A: If you did not observe duplicates or downstream problems, no action is required. If you did, choose Option A for reconciliation data or Option B for guided replay.
